chunks: He said: Abul Hasan Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Maythami reported to me, he said: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn al-Mustanir narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Mus'ab narrated to us, he said: Abbad ibn Ya'qub narrated to us, he said: Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Mas'udi narrated to us, from Kathir al-Nawwa, from Abu Maryam al-Khawlani, from Malik ibn Damra, he said: The Commander of the Faithful Ali ibn Abi Talib, peace be upon him, said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family, took my hand and said:

Whoever follows these five [prayers] and then dies loving you has fulfilled his covenant. And whoever dies hating you has died a death of pre-Islamic ignorance; he will be held accountable for what he did in Islam. And whoever lives after you loving you, Allah will seal his life with security and faith until he reaches me at the Pond.

key_terms.الحَوْض: Al-Hawd — the Pond; the basin from which the Prophet will give drink on the Day of Judgment
key_terms.ميتة جاهلية: Mitat al-Jahiliyyah — death of pre-Islamic ignorance; dying without true faith
key_terms.نَحْب: Nahb — covenant, vow; to fulfill one's pledge or obligation to God

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad say about loving or hating Imam Ali?
ai.summary: The Commander of the Faithful, Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (AS), relates that the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) took his hand and made a profound declaration about three categories of people: one who follows the five daily prayers and dies loving Ali has fulfilled his covenant with God; one who dies hating Ali has died a death of pre-Islamic ignorance and will be held accountable for whatever good he did in Islam; and one who lives after Ali while loving him will have his life sealed with security and faith until he reaches the Prophet at the Pond (al-Hawd) on the Day of Judgment. Narrated through a chain going back to Malik ibn Damra, this hadith was delivered in a gathering where the Prophet publicly took Ali by the hand, establishing love of Ali as a criterion for the acceptance of faith.
